title: Arma Reforger dedicated server config (server.json / config.json)
$comment: Hand-written, derived from docs/en/ArmaReforger_ServerConfig_EN.md §4 (hard rules) and §5 (parameter reference), build 1.6.0.119 / engine 192142. Coverage against data/server-keys.json is enforced by tools/check-schema-coverage.mjs, so a key added to the document without being added here fails `npm run check`. additionalProperties:false is deliberate and is the point of this schema: an unknown key is the most common real failure (a typo such as `maxplayers`, or a field name from before 0.9.8.73). Keys that exist in the 1.6.0.119 schema but are NOT publicly documented are listed explicitly, with "undocumented": true in their description, so that a config known to work does not fail validation. Severity is decided by tools/validate-server-config.mjs, not here: the game clamps some out-of-range values (ports, game.name) with a log line instead of refusing to start, so those are reported as warnings.

bindAddress.description: IP the game socket binds to. Empty means 0.0.0.0. IPv6 is not supported. Section 5.1.

bindPort.description: UDP port of the game socket. Better omitted: it is taken equal to publicPort. Section 5.1.

publicAddress.description: IP registered with the backend. Empty = auto-detect (recommended). Accepts the literal "local" (not verified). A public IP here breaks joining from the server's own LAN when the router lacks NAT hairpin; a 192.168.x.x value here makes the server unreachable from the internet. Section 5.1.

publicPort.description: UDP port registered with the backend. Behind NAT this is the external forwarding port. Section 5.1.

a2s.description: Steam Query section. Optional — omit it entirely if unused. Section 5.2.

address.description: Required. IP the A2S socket binds to; a real working config uses "0.0.0.0". Section 5.2.

port.description: UDP port for A2S queries. Out of range is not fatal: the log gets "[A2S] Invalid port, set to default=17777...". Section 5.2.

rcon.description: Bohemia's own remote console (RCONProtocol in the server binary). Entirely optional. NOT BattlEye RCON, which is configured in battleye/BEServer_x64.cfg. Section 5.3.

address.description: Required. IP the RCON socket binds to. Use 127.0.0.1 on any internet-facing server: RCON grants full control and is protected by the password alone. Section 5.3.

port.description: RCON port. The protocol (UDP or TCP) is unconfirmed — sources disagree. Out of range is not fatal: "[RCON] Invalid port, set to default=19999...". Section 5.3.

password.description: Required for RCON to start. No spaces, at least 3 characters. Section 5.3.

maxClients.description: Maximum simultaneous RCON clients. A killed client holds its slot for 45 seconds unless it sends @logout. Section 5.3.

permission.description: Maps to ERCONPermissions. monitor can only run #players; admin can run #restart, #shutdown, #kick, #ban. There is no finer granularity. Section 5.3.

whitelist.description: If set, only the listed commands are allowed. Section 5.3.

name.description: Server name in the browser. A longer name is cropped, not rejected: "Session name exceed max value > N, cropped under limit...". Section 5.4.

password.description: Password to connect. Empty means no password. Section 5.4.

passwordAdmin.description: Administrator password, used in game as `#login <password>`. No spaces. Section 5.4.

admins.description: identityId and/or steamId of administrators. Since 1.3.0 no more than 20 unique IDs. The priority join queue works only for IdentityId. Section 5.4.

scenarioId.description: Path to the scenario .conf together with its resource GUID, e.g. {ECC61978EDCC2B5A}Missions/23_Campaign.conf. Take the string from data/scenarios.json — never invent a GUID. For a mod mission the GUID comes from <Mission>.conf.meta, field Name. Section 4 rule 1.

visible.description: Show the server in the browser (true since 0.9.8.73). Section 5.4.

crossPlatform.description: If true, PLATFORM_PC, PLATFORM_XBL and PLATFORM_PSN are added to supportedPlatforms automatically. Section 5.4.

supportedPlatforms.description: Allowed combinations: PC alone; PC + Xbox + PlayStation; and on a MODDED server PC + Xbox (PlayStation is never added there). Not allowed: PC + Xbox on a vanilla server, PC + PlayStation, Xbox alone, PlayStation alone, Xbox + PlayStation. Section 4 rule 7 and §5.5.1.

modsRequiredByDefault.description: The default `required` value for every entry in mods[]. Section 5.4.

mods.description: Mod list. The game exports this array itself: mods menu -> Saved mod settings -> JSON tab. That exported text is a bare list of objects with NO surrounding array — wrap it in square brackets before pasting, or the config fails schema validation. Section 5.4.1.

modId.description: The mod's GUID from addon.gproj, line `GUID "..."`, with braces and dashes stripped, exactly 16 hex characters. Not the project ID. The key is modId, not the wiki's modID. Section 4 rules 2-3.

name.description: Affects nothing — a human-readable comment. Section 5.4.1.

version.description: Optional. If absent, the latest version of the mod is taken. Section 5.4.1.

required.description: If false and the mod cannot be downloaded from the Workshop, it is removed from the list with a warning. Default comes from game.modsRequiredByDefault. Section 5.4.1.

gameInstanceFiles.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Do not specify it. Section 5.4.

fileReferences.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Do not specify it. Section 5.4.

loadSessionSave.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

keepSessionSave.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

saveRetention.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

autoSaveInterval.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

hiveId.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

databases.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Server persistent storage; not needed for an ordinary server. A `storages` entry references these by name — a mismatch logs `Storage "X" contains undefined database named "Y"!`. Section 5.7.

storages.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

preset.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

options.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

database.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.7.

lobbyPlayerSynchronise.description: Send the list of present players to GameAPI with the heartbeat. Removes the mismatch between the real and the displayed player count. Section 5.6.

disableCrashReporter.description: Disable automatic crash reports. The analogue of the -disableCrashReporter parameter. Section 5.6.

disableNavmeshStreaming.description: Disable navmesh streaming: the navmesh is held in memory (better AI response, hundreds of MB more RAM). An empty array disables it for everything; with a list, only for those projects. Was a boolean before 1.2.0 — on 1.6.0.119 it is an array. Section 5.6.

disableServerShutdown.description: Do not shut the server down when the connection to the backend is lost. Section 5.6.

disableAI.description: Disable AI completely: no AIWorld is created or ticked. Section 5.6.

aiLimit.description: Upper limit on the number of AIs; a negative value means no limit. Overridden by the -aiLimit startup parameter. Section 5.6.

slotReservationTimeout.description: Seconds to hold a slot for a kicked player; the minimum value disables it. Works only for kicks by replication. Section 5.6.

maxSize.description: Maximum people in the queue; 0 disables the queue. Section 5.6.

heartbeat.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Section 5.6.

serverId.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Do not specify it. Section 5.1.

ownerType.description: undocumented: present in the 1.6.0.119 schema, not publicly documented. Do not specify it. Section 5.1.

serverMaxViewDistance.description: Draw distance on the server. Section 5.5.

serverMinGrassDistance.description: Minimum grass distance in metres. Only 0 (do not force it on clients) or 50..150 — values 1..49 are not allowed. Section 4 rule 4 and §5.5.

networkViewDistance.description: Maximum network transmission distance for replicated entities. Section 5.5.

fastValidation.description: Fast check that the map state matches between client and server. Always true for a public server; false only for local development. Section 5.5.

battlEye.description: Enable the BattlEye anti-cheat. Often set to false in a real config to reduce load. Section 5.5.

VONDisableUI.description: Disable the voice chat interface. Section 5.5.

VONDisableDirectSpeechUI.description: Disable the direct speech interface. Section 5.5.

VONCanTransmitCrossFaction.description: true — transmit on other factions' radio; false — listen only. Section 5.5.

missionHeader.description: Overrides fields of the scenario's mission header class. Keys are class field names (m_*), typed by the game: an unsupported type logs "Server Config MissionHeader: Parameter 'X' is not supported type!" and is then ignored — this does not bring the server down. Which keys are accepted depends on the header class of the scenario: Conflict uses SCR_MissionHeaderCampaign (base fields + campaign fields), Game Master uses SCR_MissionHeader (base fields only), Combat Ops uses SCR_MissionHeaderCombatOps. A key from a foreign class is silently ignored. Values written as 0/1 in scenario .conf files must be true/false here. Known keys, their types and their classes: data/mission-header-fields.json. Section 5.5.2 and docs/en/ArmaReforger_MissionHeader_EN.md.
